title: Trophic Ecology of the Blacktip Shark, Carcharhinus limbatus (Valencienees, 1839), in the Mexican Caribbean Sea
content:
ABSTRACT

This study examines the trophic ecology of the blacktip shark, Carcharhinus limbatus, in the Mexican Caribbean Sea using δ13C and δ15N stable isotope analyses to evaluate seasonal and sex-based variation in trophic niches and prey contributions. A total of 37 individuals were sampled during 2023 in Bahía Espíritu Santo, Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve. δ13C values ranged from −13.89‰ to −8.57‰, whereas δ15N values ranged from 10.80‰ to 14.67‰. Median δ13C values did not differ significantly between seasons or sexes; however, δ15N values were significantly higher during the rainy season (median = 13.21‰) than during the dry season (11.73‰), suggesting consumption of higher-trophic-level prey during the reproductive period. Trophic niche width, represented by SEAc, was greater during the rainy season (SEAc = 1.32‰2) than during the dry season (SEAc = 0.58‰2), suggesting greater trophic diversity and availability of food resources during the rainy season. Overlap between female and male isotopic niches was also observed, with females overlapping 54% of the male niche and males overlapping 85% of the female niche, suggesting similar habitat use and food resources between sexes. MixSIAR models indicated that crustaceans were the most important dietary source in C. limbatus muscle tissue (50.8%), followed by coastal fishes (15.9%) and rays (13.7%). C. limbatus exhibited a flexible and opportunistic feeding strategy that may be influenced by prey availability across climatic seasons and by habitat characteristics. Our findings suggest high trophic plasticity in C. limbatus and highlight the importance of incorporating seasonal variability and habitat characterization into assessments of its trophic ecology to support effective management and conservation strategies for this species in the Caribbean Sea.
